First things first, I bumped the budget up to $400 to account for a 1-year online gaming subscription. As for your requirements: Windows 10 might be free for system builders in the future, but in the meantime, there's Linux/piracy/educational programs for students/cheap keys from online marketplaces if you must have Windows (this will add $50). A full-price Windows key pushes the build over budget though, sorry. You can pick up a keyboard and mouse for $15 or maybe even less at a local store. Now for the builds.

[Exhibit A: $364 without keyboard and mouse and operating system](http://www.reddit.com/r/CabaloftheBuildsmiths/wiki/usbuilds)

[Exhibit B: $400 without keyboard and mouse and operating system - website only goes down to $400](http://choosemypc.net/build/?budget=400&oc=false&options=)

First build uses a 270, second a 270X. Reviews and benchmarks here: [1](http://www.anandtech.com/show/7503/the-amd-radeon-r9-270x-270-review-feat-asus-his/15) [2](http://www.tomshardware.co.uk/radeon-r9-270-review-benchmarks,review-32824.html)

As you can see, both cards can maintain at least: 

* 1080p 60fps high settings on a popular first-person shooter (not 6 months old, but I prefer using popular titles for benchmarks; it's also harder to find benchmarks for games other than the ones used by every website). 

* 1080p 60 fps medium settings, 45 fps high settings on a well-known graphics-intensive game

* 1080p 45fps high settings on a popular survival horror game

* 1080p 60fps ultra quality on a critically acclaimed narrative-driven game

* 1080p 50 fps ultra quality on a popular action-adventure game

* 1080p 53 fps high quality on a well-known real-time strategy game

In conclusion, we can see that although I have failed to provide a 'console killer' for the same price as a console, for just $50-$100 more (money that will be saved by not paying for online services every year), you can build a pretty decent rig for 1080p 60fps at high settings.
